issues.issue: What date is used to assess whether a claimant still has third-country status under Article 1E?
issues.applicant_position: The date must be fluid, covering status up to the hearing; the application judge's first step wrongly fixed the date.
issues.respondent_position: Agreed the date must be fluid and that status is assessed up to the hearing; no debate on this issue.
issues.result_quote: an inquiry regarding whether a claimant should be excluded under Article 1E should take into account all relevant facts to the date of the hearing

issues.issue: What test applies where a claimant lost third-country status, including through asylum shopping?
issues.applicant_position: Asylum shopping can justify exclusion even after status is lost, in limited cases; the test should reflect this.
issues.respondent_position: The true issue is protection need at the hearing; exclusion should not apply where status was voluntarily forfeited.
issues.result_quote: If the answer is yes, the RPD must consider and balance various factors.

issues.issue: Did the RPD reasonably find that the respondents still held Chilean permanent residence at the hearing?
issues.applicant_position: Respondents held Chilean permanent residence at the hearing, so Article 1E applies; the RPD finding is reasonable and deserves deference.
issues.respondent_position: Status may have lapsed after more than a year abroad without renewal; the RPD should have examined that possibility.
issues.result_quote: the respondents possessed status in Chile is a factual finding to which deference is owed
